precepts.text: Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign; according to all that he hath done shall ye do; the man is the sign, not his wife.
precepts.point: Take counsel together and it shall come to nought, for God is with us, Immanuel: once the child was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

precepts.text: When Israel is in the midst of sin, God uses this language in the female context: she hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her. Definition read in class: scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, and informally a despised, immoral, or worthless person. That is the word God chose for his own people when the wickedness would not come out. Self examine, so that word never describes you.
precepts.point: She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and in her tongue is the law of kindness. This is the kind of wife you want. There was no kindness or wisdom in that email. Brothers, be mindful who you marry.
precepts.why:
“She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is the kind of wife you want, brothers. There was no kindness or wisdom in the email that attacked leadership over the one instance of a leader put out for adultery, while ignoring the three bishops and the seven or eight deacons who were in the midst of no such thing. For every solution we try to give, that spirit has two problems. That is not wife material; they are idolatrous women, some of them idolatrous evil black women, and they will try to destroy your life. Be mindful who you marry.

Now see what language God uses when Israel is in the midst of sin; he uses it in the female context: “She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her”. There is one word that is often wanted but is hurtful to say, so God says it. Your scum is still in your mouth, sisters.

Scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, such as pond scum or soap scum. Informally it means a despised, immoral or worthless person or group, the scum of the earth. The slang meaning goes further: the epitome of a worthless, good-for-nothing human, at the bottom of the hierarchy of humans, possibly the worst word you can have your name associated with. It describes someone so disgraceful they are seen as the lowest form of life: worthlessness, a waste of skin, dirt, nothing. Because it is perfectly acceptable English and not a swear, it is even more demeaning; it is used only when it is the only word for the job, and it makes the victim feel like the lowest of the low.

That is the word God chose for his own people when she wore herself out with lies and the wickedness would not come out of her. Some of these evil sisters are the scum of the earth; that is what God is saying. So examine yourself, and open your mouth with wisdom and the law of kindness instead.

precepts.text: Make no mourning for the dead; the Most High took Ezekiel's wife and he was not to weep for her.
precepts.point: The same standard fell on Jehoiakim the son of Josiah: they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my brother, or, Ah lord.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
Aaron, Eleazar and Ithamar were told, “Uncover not your heads, neither rend your clothes; lest ye die, and lest wrath come upon all the people.” Basically they were told not to mourn for Nadab and Abihu, because they died in the midst of sin and what they did was abominable to the Most High.

Ezekiel is the example of that word. “Son of man, behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke: yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down. Forbear to cry, make no mourning for the dead, bind the tire of thine head upon thee, and put on thy shoes upon thy feet, and cover not thy lips, and eat not the bread of men.”

The Most High took away the desire of his eyes, his wife, with a stroke, and he was not to weep for her. “So I spake unto the people in the morning: and at even my wife died; and I did in the morning as I was commanded.” Ezekiel went and taught the people that morning, and at even his wife died, and he made no mourning, just as the priests were commanded.

precepts.text: The Most High warned that a nation from far, whose tongue we understand not, would besiege us in all our gates, the curse that had to be inflicted once we went too far.
precepts.point: Because her filthiness is lewdness and He purged her yet she was not purged, she shall not be purged from her filthiness anymore until He has caused His fury to rest upon her. He will not go back, nor spare, nor repent; there is no more sackcloth or fasting to turn Him back at this point.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

precepts.why:
“Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great.” The Most High does not merely cook it and let the flame die; He stacks the wood and keeps it lit, “Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh”, so we cook long and well, and then sets the pot empty on the coals till the brass is hot and the scum consumed.

Moses warned this was coming. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. That nation eats the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land “until thou be destroyed”, and “shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst”.

That is the curse that had to be inflicted once we went too far. “I have purged thee, and thou wast not purged”, so she “shalt not be purged from thy filthiness any more, till I have caused my fury to rest upon thee.” He will not go back, nor spare, nor repent; there is no more sackcloth or fasting to turn Him back at this point. The nation from far, whose tongue we understood not, besieging us in all our gates, is the fire under the pot.

precepts.text: The Most High took the wife away because such things cause even prophets of understanding to fall away from Him.
precepts.point: Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening his wife died, and he did in the morning as he was commanded. This shows the life of a prophet, whose purpose is above family, love, and children, so when a wife or a distraction interferes with the work the Most High assigned, the purpose comes first.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

precepts.why:
The Most High takes away “the desire of thine eyes with a stroke”, Ezekiel's wife, and tells him not to mourn or weep. Why take the wife? “Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.”

Such things cause even prophets of understanding to fall away from Him. This is the life of a prophet, whose purpose is above family, love and children. Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, “and at even my wife died”, and he did in the morning as he was commanded: bound his tire, put on his shoes, covered not his lips and ate not the bread of men.

When a wife or a distraction interferes with the work the Most High assigned, the purpose comes first.

precepts.text: Paul urged the single life so that a man may attend upon the Most High without distraction, which is exactly what the Most High secured for Ezekiel.
precepts.point: Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening his wife died, and he did in the morning as he was commanded. This shows the life of a prophet, whose purpose is above family, love, and children, so when a wife or a distraction interferes with the work the Most High assigned, the purpose comes first.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

precepts.why:
Paul urged the single life: “this I speak for your own profit; not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is comely, and that ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction.”

Attending upon the Lord without distraction is exactly what the Most High secured for Ezekiel. He took away the desire of his eyes with a stroke, and told him to forbear to cry and make no mourning for the dead, so that the prophet went on with the work he was assigned. He spoke to the people in the morning, his wife died at even, and “I did in the morning as I was commanded.”

The purpose of a prophet is above family, love and children. When a wife or a distraction interferes with the work, the purpose comes first.

precepts.text: The prophet and the children the Most High gave him are set for signs and wonders in Israel, as He used prophets, their wives, and their children to picture what would come upon the nation.
precepts.point: They shall do as Ezekiel did, not covering their lips nor eating the bread of men, but pining away for their iniquities and mourning to one another. Ezekiel is a sign to them, and when it comes they shall know that He is the Lord God.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign”. Isaiah says the same of himself: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.”

The Most High used His prophets, their wives and their children to picture what would come upon the nation. Just as Ezekiel's wife was the desire of his eyes, the beautiful temple was the desire of the nation's eyes: “I will profane my sanctuary, the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and that which your soul pitieth”. Their sons and daughters would fall by the sword, and they would do as Ezekiel did, not covering their lips nor eating the bread of men, but pining away for their iniquities and mourning one toward another.

The word is “according to all that he hath done shall ye do”. The prophet and his family are the sign, and when it comes, they shall know that He is the Lord God.

points: In the ninth year, tenth month, and tenth day, the word of the Most High comes on the very day the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem, and Ezekiel is told to write the name of the day and utter a parable to the rebellious house.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: He is told to set on a pot, pour in water, and gather the pieces, the thigh and the shoulder and the choice bones, taking the choice of the flock and burning the bones under it to make it boil well. This pictures Babylon taking out the best of our mighty men and leaders first.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein; He calls the choice pieces, the best of the Israelites we looked up to, scum, because of the laws we broke. The Most High will call you something you do not want to be called.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: Her blood is in the midst of her, set upon the top of a rock and not poured on the ground to be covered, so that it might cause fury to come up and take vengeance.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: Woe to the bloody city: the Most High will make the pile for fire great, heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, spice it well, and let the bones be burnt, then set the empty pot on the coals till the brass is hot and the scum consumed. He does not merely cook it and let the flame die; He stacks the wood and keeps it lit so we cook long and well.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: Because her filthiness is lewdness and He purged her yet she was not purged, she shall not be purged from her filthiness anymore until He has caused His fury to rest upon her. He will not go back, nor spare, nor repent; there is no more sackcloth or fasting to turn Him back at this point.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: The Most High tells Ezekiel He will take away the desire of his eyes with a stroke, yet he must not mourn, weep, or make mourning for the dead; he is to bind his tire, put on his shoes, cover not his lips, and eat not the bread of men.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening his wife died, and he did in the morning as he was commanded. This shows the life of a prophet, whose purpose is above family, love, and children, so when a wife or a distraction interferes with the work the Most High assigned, the purpose comes first.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: When the people ask what these things mean to them, Ezekiel answers that the Most High will profane His sanctuary, the excellency of their strength and the desire of their eyes, and their sons and daughters shall fall by the sword. Just as his wife was the desire of his eyes, the beautiful temple was the desire of the nation's eyes.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: They shall do as Ezekiel did, not covering their lips nor eating the bread of men, but pining away for their iniquities and mourning to one another. Ezekiel is a sign to them, and when it comes they shall know that He is the Lord God.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: In the day the Most High takes from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and their sons and daughters, one that escapes shall come to Ezekiel to bring the report with his own ears.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

points: In that day Ezekiel's mouth shall be opened to the one who escaped, and he shall be no more dumb but a sign unto them, that they may know He is the Lord. When it comes to pass they will come spooked and shocked, and he will tell them the Most High had told them.
